paths.description: Public authentication entry after the servicos.acesso.gov.br redirect; covers CPF and alternative-method selection, invalid CPF recovery, desktop/mobile/preferences, no-JS, security, performance and memory single-state evidence. Authenticated routes, real credential submission, bank/certificate handoffs and account management were not covered because no safe test identity was supplied.

findings.summary: The login page does not follow the system dark theme.
findings.evidence: The dark-preference screenshot remains a white surface, and computed color-scheme is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark tokens with accessible contrast.

findings.summary: The login page has no meta description.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe and Lighthouse both report a descriptive title but no meta[name=description].
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise description of the gov.br sign-in purpose while retaining noindex if indexing is intentionally disallowed.

findings.summary: State changes are not enhanced with View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM contains accordion/modal state changes, while the animation probe found no animations and source inspection found no transition setup.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for meaningful accordion or authentication-state changes, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Bank and QR overlays use custom modal scripting rather than native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: Rendered source loads modal.js and invokes showModal(...) from a button; no dialog or popover element is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal flows or popover for transient UI, with native focus management and light dismiss.

findings.summary: Several bank controls are too small and lose visible keyboard focus.
findings.evidence: The focus probe measured bank buttons around 27px high with outline none, while the primary mobile controls are 40px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44x44 CSS-pixel targets where practical and a strong :focus-visible style for every bank option.

findings.summary: Invalid CPF input gives no visible or programmatic recovery feedback.
findings.evidence: After entering 123 and invoking Continue, aria-invalid remained false and no alert/error text appeared.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, set aria-invalid, associate specific guidance with aria-describedby, and announce it in a live region.

findings.summary: The authentication entry is very slow to become visible.
findings.evidence: Trace measured FCP 11.8s and LCP 13.0s; Lighthouse measured FCP 20.0s and LCP 20.5s on a cold mobile run.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the redirect/challenge chain and prioritize the login HTML/CSS; remove avoidable pre-content delay.

findings.summary: The simple login journey has a heavy, redirect-rich resource load.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 72 requests and 1.73 MB transferred, including 1.18 MB of scripts and multiple render-blocking stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Split and defer non-critical scripts, cache hashed assets, self-host/trim fonts, and shorten the redirect dependency chain.

findings.summary: Large JavaScript dominates the login load.
findings.evidence: The HAR identifies a 783,542-byte portal bundle plus challenge, hCaptcha, government-bar, jQuery and other scripts before login.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit coverage, remove unused legacy code, and conditionally load secondary authentication dependencies only when selected.

findings.summary: The visible CPF label is not associated with the CPF input.
findings.evidence: DOM shows label for="cpf" but the input id is accountId; the probe reports no associated label.
findings.suggestedFix: Make label[for] exactly match the input id and verify the accessible name in the accessibility tree.

findings.summary: The bank-login option fails minimum text contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 4.37:1 for green #008c32 text and the inverse badge, below the 4.5:1 requirement.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the green or adjust the background so normal text and badge text meet WCAG AA.

findings.summary: The page starts its heading hierarchy at h3 and some focusable bank controls have no visible outline.
findings.evidence: The probe found only h3 headings and several bank buttons with outline none; Lighthouse accessibility was 0.73.
findings.suggestedFix: Use an h1 for the page purpose, a logical hierarchy, and consistent :focus-visible styling.

findings.summary: The viewport explicitly prevents pinch zoom.
findings.evidence: The rendered meta viewport contains maximum-scale=1.0 and user-scalable=0.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable restrictions so users can zoom.

findings.summary: The login load emits console and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse records CSP-blocked hCaptcha requests and missing rawline-900 font files.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the hCaptcha CSP allowlist and font URLs, then verify a clean console.

findings.summary: Rendered images omit intrinsic width and height attributes.
findings.evidence: DOM source shows the main logo and hero image without width/height attributes even though natural dimensions are known.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width and height attributes and retain responsive CSS sizing.

findings.summary: Deprecated browser behavior and a legacy library remain in the authentication page.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags an unload listener and deprecated Protected Audience API use; the HAR also loads jQuery 2.2.4.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unload handlers, update third-party dependencies, and replace or isolate legacy jQuery usage.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP policy are weaker than expected for an identity provider.
findings.evidence: Cookie evidence shows two TS cookies without Secure/HttpOnly and SameSite=None; the observed CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark every sensitive cookie Secure, HttpOnly and appropriately SameSite; move inline code to nonce/hash CSP and remove unsafe-eval.

findings.summary: Several browser defense headers are absent or weak.
findings.evidence: Header probe did not observe nosniff, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy; CSP uses frame-ancestors but also broad unsafe script allowances.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff, a strict Referrer-Policy and minimal Permissions-Policy, then tighten CSP without breaking required authentication providers.

findings.summary: The login UI is an empty JavaScript shell for non-JavaScript clients.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 0% content coverage with an empty #root; the crawler view says only “You need to enable JavaScript”.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the login entry and keep a functional HTML form as the baseline, then enhance it with JavaScript.

findings.summary: The representative 404 response offers no recovery path.
findings.evidence: The robots.txt request returned HTTP 404 and a page containing only “Erro: 404 Not Found” beneath the site header.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide an explanatory error state with safe links back to login/help and retry guidance where relevant.

findings.summary: The CPF sign-in field disables useful identity autofill semantics.
findings.evidence: The CPF input uses autocomplete="new-password" despite being an account identifier.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the appropriate username autocomplete token while retaining numeric inputmode and privacy safeguards.

findings.summary: Resource cost is disproportionate to the first login step.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 1.73 MB, 72 requests, 35 images and 827 KB attributed to cross-origin requests before authentication.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy/conditional-load provider assets and hCaptcha, trim icon/font sets, and keep only resources needed for the selected method.
